questions.sentence: The man ___ lives next door is a doctor.
questions.explanation: 'Who' is used for people; here 'the man' is the subject of 'lives'

questions.sentence: The book ___ I read was interesting.
questions.explanation: 'Which' or 'that' is used for things; 'the book' is a thing

questions.sentence: The city ___ I was born is beautiful.
questions.explanation: 'Where' replaces 'in which' for places

questions.sentence: The day ___ we met was special.
questions.explanation: 'When' replaces 'on which/in which' for time

questions.sentence: The reason ___ I called was important.
questions.explanation: 'Why' is used after 'the reason'

questions.sentence: The woman which called is my aunt.
questions.correct_answer: The woman who called is my aunt.
questions.grammar_rule: 'Who' for people, 'which' for things - never mix them
questions.grammar_rule_uz: Shaxslar uchun 'who', narsalar uchun 'which' - aralashtirib bo'lmaydi
questions.explanation: Use 'who' (not 'which') when referring to people

questions.sentence: My sister, ___ lives in Paris, is visiting us.
questions.grammar_rule: Non-defining clauses: Use 'who' (not 'that') for people, with commas
questions.grammar_rule_uz: Aniqlamaydigan gaplar: Shaxslar uchun 'who' (emas 'that'), vergul bilan
questions.explanation: Non-defining clause (with commas) uses 'who', never 'that'

questions.sentence: This is the teacher ___ class I attended.
questions.explanation: 'Whose' shows possession: 'whose class' = 'his/her class'

questions.original_sentence: I met a girl. Her father works at the bank.
questions.correct_answer: I met a girl whose father works at the bank.
questions.explanation: 'Her father' → 'whose father' to connect the sentences

questions.sentence: The man ___ I spoke to was helpful.
questions.explanation: 'Whom' is used when the person is the object (I spoke to HIM)

questions.sentence: London, that is the capital of England, is very old.
questions.correct_answer: London, which is the capital of England, is very old.
questions.grammar_rule: Non-defining clauses: Never use 'that', use 'which' or 'who'
questions.explanation: Non-defining clauses (with commas) cannot use 'that'

questions.sentence: The hotel, ___ we stayed, was excellent.
questions.explanation: 'Where' is used for places in both defining and non-defining clauses

questions.instruction: Combine using 'which' referring to the whole clause
questions.original_sentence: He passed the exam. This surprised everyone.
questions.correct_answer: He passed the exam, which surprised everyone.
hints: 'Which' can refer to the whole previous clause
questions.grammar_rule: 'Which' can refer to an entire previous clause
questions.grammar_rule_uz: 'Which' oldingi butun gapga murojaat qilishi mumkin
questions.explanation: 'Which' here refers to the fact that he passed, not just 'the exam'

questions.sentence: That's the house ___ roof was damaged in the storm.
questions.grammar_rule: 'Whose' can be used for things as well as people
questions.grammar_rule_uz: 'Whose' narsalar uchun ham, shaxslar uchun ham ishlatiladi
questions.explanation: 'Whose' shows possession for both people AND things

questions.sentence: The man to ___ I gave the letter is my boss.
questions.explanation: Formal: preposition + whom (to whom, with whom, for whom)

questions.sentence: The information what I received was incorrect.
questions.correct_answer: The information which/that I received was incorrect.
questions.grammar_rule: Never use 'what' as a relative pronoun; use 'which/that'
questions.explanation: 'What' = 'the thing which', so don't use it after a noun
After quantifiers like 'all', 'everything', prefer 'that'

questions.original_sentence: The man who is standing there is my uncle.
questions.correct_answer: The man standing there is my uncle.
questions.grammar_rule: Defining relative clauses can be reduced using participles
questions.grammar_rule_uz: Aniqlovchi gaplar sifatdosh bilan qisqartirilishi mumkin
questions.explanation: 'Who is standing' → 'standing' (reduced relative clause)

questions.sentence: The thing ___ annoys me is his attitude.
questions.grammar_rule_uz: 'The thing/only thing/first thing' dan keyin 'that' afzal
questions.explanation: After 'thing', 'that' is preferred over 'which'

questions.original_sentence: This is the way. We solve problems in this way.
questions.correct_answer: This is the way in which we solve problems.
hints: Can also use 'that' or no pronoun
questions.grammar_rule: 'The way in which/that/Ø' = how something is done
questions.grammar_rule_uz: 'The way in which/that/Ø' = qanday qilinishini bildiradi
questions.explanation: 'In which' is formal; can also say 'the way we solve' or 'the way that we solve'
